title: Quickstarts: add route naming conventions + validate spend in Console Usage Insights
author: Wei Chen
description:
Context: With “In-console usage insights (cost drivers by route)” landing behind a flag, we need quickstarts to (1) show how to set a stable `route` identifier and (2) show how to confirm the route shows up as a cost driver in the Console.

What’s in this PR: 1) Adds a short “Route tagging” section to the primary quickstarts (Node + Python) showing how to set a route identifier, plus naming conventions and cardinality do’s/don’ts. 2) Adds a “Validate costs in Console” section (step-by-step) that points devs to Usage Insights → Routes, shows what to expect for “Unknown route”, and how to reconcile “why does this not match invoice exactly?” at a high level. 3) Updates sample code to use stable, low-cardinality route names and avoids dynamic values.

Route naming guidance (tl;dr): - Use stable, semantic, low-cardinality strings: `chat.completions`, `support.reply`, `search.rerank` - If you have environments, suffix once: `chat.completions:prod` (or use env filter in Console; prefer filters over encoding env into route) - Don’t include user IDs, request IDs, raw URLs, or prompt hashes - Keep it short; avoid unbounded path params (`/users/:id/...`) and prefer logical operation names.

Console validation steps added to quickstarts: - Make a few requests with `route` set - Open Console → Usage Insights → Routes - Filter by environment/region if needed - Confirm the route appears (or see “Unknown route” if missing) - Click into route detail to see model breakdown + p50/p95 - Export CSV/JSON for a bounded time range if Finance/FinOps needs it.

Notes: The exact SDK surface differs slightly by language; the quickstarts use the recommended client option where available, and fall back to the standardized header for raw HTTP examples.

Example snippet included (Node): `const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); await client.chat.completions.create({ model: "redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct", route: "chat.completions", messages: [...] });`

Example snippet included (Python): `client = Redwood(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"]) client.chat.completions.create(model="redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct", route="chat.completions", messages=[...])`

Testing: - Ran quickstarts locally (node + python) - Lint/format - Verified the new markdown renders properly in README.

Rollout: Docs/quickstarts content only; no product flag dependencies.

Screenshots: N/A (we link to Console docs; keeping quickstarts repo lightweight).

review_conversation: Elliot Price: Can we add one line explaining why invoice totals might not match route totals (freshness/late-arriving metering)? Keep it short but preempt support tickets.
Wei Chen (author): Added a short “Why might totals differ?” paragraph in the validation section with a link to the main docs FAQ. Kept it non-alarming and avoided deep billing details.
Monica Patel: For Node, the snippet uses `route` option (good), but for the raw fetch example can we include the standardized header name explicitly? People copy/paste that.
Wei Chen (author): Yep — added `X-Redwood-Route: chat.completions` to the curl + fetch snippets and noted that SDK route param maps to the same underlying header.
Paula Mendes: Please align naming examples with the PRD: use `chat.completions` / `embeddings.create` rather than URL-like strings. Also call out “Unknown route” as a symptom of not tagging.
Wei Chen (author): Updated all examples to operation-style names and added a short “If you see Unknown route” troubleshooting line in the Console validation steps.
Felix Schneider: Minor: in the “Validate costs” section, can you mention filtering by time range and that it can take a bit for new data to show up (ingestion lag)?
Wei Chen (author): Added: “select last 15m/1h; allow a few minutes for ingestion” and kept it generic (no hard SLO numbers).
Elliot Price: LGTM after the FAQ link add.
